title: Uni-XAS: Alignment-Driven Bidirectional Multimodal Learning for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
authors: Suyang Zhong, Yuhao Zhao, Boying Huang, Fanjie Xu, Pengwei Xu, Haoyi Tao, Xi Fang, Jun Cheng, Fujie Tang
abstract: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a key technique for probing local atomic environments, yet learning based modeling must bridge two heterogeneous modalities: 1D continuous spectra and 3D atomic structures. Existing approaches typically decouple forward spectrum prediction and inverse structure inference into separate regression tasks, hindering shared representation learning. Moreover, severe permutation ambiguity among identical atoms often limits inverse modeling to coarse structure descriptors rather than explicit 3D structure generation. In this work, we present Uni-XAS, a unified benchmark and learning framework that reframes bidirectional XAS modeling as a cross-modal alignment and conditional generation problem. We first propose XASLip, an alignment recipe coupling a physics-aware spectral encoder with an absorberaware manifold optimization strategy to resolve fine-grained intra-element coordination variations. Building upon this shared latent space, we formulate forward prediction as anchored absolute-spectrum generation via retrieval-augmented decoding, effectively preventing physical scale collapse and energy drift. For the inherently ill-posed inverse problem, we introduce Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching, which integrates type-wise optimal transport into a continuous generative flow to provide a principled solution to ligand permutation ambiguity without relying on heavy high-order equivariant architectures. Evaluated on a largescale standardized benchmark of 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs, Uni-XAS demonstrates strong performance in cross-modal retrieval, accurate absolute-spectrum prediction, and composition-conditional 3D structure generation, establishing a scalable, reproducible, and protocol-consistent foundation for multimodal learning and standardized evaluation in scientific spectroscopy.
summary: This paper introduces Uni-XAS, a unified machine learning framework designed to solve the challenging bidirectional problem in X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS). It overcomes limitations of prior methods by treating spectral and structural inference as a single cross-modal alignment task. The resulting framework achieves state-of-the-art performance across retrieval, forward prediction, and inverse structure generation on a massive dataset.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a unified machine learning framework for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS) that can consistently bridge the gap between heterogeneous 1D spectral data and 3D local atomic structures.
main_result: Uni-XAS establishes a scalable, reproducible benchmark demonstrating strong performance in cross-modal retrieval, accurate absolute-spectrum prediction, and composition-conditional 3D structure generation.
method: The authors propose reframing the bidirectional problem as a cross-modal alignment and conditional generation task using specialized components like XASLip for alignment and Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching (PR-Flow) for inverse inference.
model_or_system: The system is X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), which probes local atomic environments by mapping between 3D local coordination geometries ($\mathbf{G}$) and continuous spectra ($\mathbf{Y}$).
key_observables: XAS spectra (1D continuous sequences) and explicit 3D coordinates defining local coordination geometry.
important_parameters: The framework utilizes a large-scale benchmark of 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs; key metrics include MAE in physical eV for energy anchors and OT-RMSD for structural fidelity.
main_assumptions: Existing methods are limited by decoupling forward/inverse tasks or failing to resolve permutation ambiguity among identical atoms. The framework assumes a shared latent space can unify these modalities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between conventional decoupled pipelines and Uni-XAS's unified approach, showing how the shared latent interface supports retrieval, RAG forward prediction, and conditional 3D local-structure generation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces Uni-XAS as a framework, detailing XASLip for alignment, followed by formulations for anchored absolute-spectrum generation (forward) and Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching (inverse). It concludes with performance evaluation on the large benchmark.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science spectroscopy, the methodology heavily relies on advanced deep learning techniques—such as generative flow matching, cross-modal alignment, and manifold optimization—which are highly relevant to developing ML models for complex physical systems beyond standard quantum computing paradigms.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Comparison of XAS modeling pipelines. (a) Forward surrogate prediction. (b) Descriptor-level inverse interpretation. (c) Uni-XAS establishes a shared latent interface supporting cross-modal retrieval, retrieval-augmented forward prediction, and conditional 3D local-structure generation.

Figure 2: Uni-XAS architecture based on a Shared Latent Space (Z). (a) XASLip Alignment: Encoders map 3D structures and 1D spectra to shared embeddings (Zs, Zy) via an absorber-aware objective. (b) Absolute-Spectrum Prediction: Query Zs retrieves spectral priors (Z) from the frozen space to augment decoding, regularized by a Latent Consistency Constraint (Lalign). (c) PR-Flow Inverse Generation: Type-wise optimal transport assigns initial noise (X0) to identical atoms to resolve permutation ambiguity. Flow trajectory (Xt) is optimized toward the aligned target (Xaligned 1 ) under retrieved structural conditioning.

Figure 3: Qualitative results of Uni-XAS. The shared latent space effectively aligns modalities to retrieve structurally consistent 3D geometries from spectral queries (A), and resolves distinct intra-element coordination numbers within the learned manifold (B). This unified interface enables accurate forward absolute-spectrum prediction (C) and high-fidelity inverse composition-conditional generation (D). Grey boxes denote absorber-centered local crops rather than periodic unit cells.
Figure 4: Statistics of the curated paired benchmark, detailing overall dataset scale, absorber distribution, and local- graph-size variability.

Figure 5: Extended qualitative examples of spectrum-to-structure retrieval across diverse absorbing elements. For each case, the input is a query spectrum (top-left). The remaining panels in the top row show the spectra associated with the retrieved candidate structures, ranked by similarity in the latent space. The bottom row visualizes the corresponding local structures: the ground-truth structure of the query (bottom-left) and the retrieved candidate structures (right). Green bounding boxes indicate the correct match among the ranked results.
